n: While Peter and John are still speaking, the priests, the captain of the temple guard, and the Sadducees confront them.

f.g: The officer in charge of the temple police, second only to the high priest in temple authority.
A priestly, aristocratic party that rejected the resurrection and angels.

n: They are irritated that the apostles are teaching the people and proclaiming resurrection from the dead through Jesus — a direct challenge to Sadducee beliefs.

f.g: grieved = greatly annoyed, disturbed.

n: They arrest Peter and John and jail them overnight, since it is already evening.

f.g: in hold = in custody.
eventide = evening.

n: Yet many who heard believed, and the number of men in the movement grows to about five thousand. Arrests can’t stop the word.
The next day the Jewish leadership assembles — rulers, elders, and scribes.

f.g: The three groups making up the Sanhedrin.

n: The high priestly family is present: Annas, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and others — the same men who condemned Jesus.

f.w: Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas

n: Placing the apostles in the center, they demand: by what power or in whose name did you do this?

f.g: A name stood for authority — whom do you represent?

n: Filled with the Holy Ghost, Peter addresses the council respectfully. Jesus had promised the Spirit would give them words in such moments.
If they are on trial for doing a kindness to a disabled man and want to know how he was healed…

f.g: impotent = powerless, disabled.
Peter notes the irony of being tried for an act of kindness.

n: …let everyone know: it was by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth — whom they crucified and God raised — that this man stands before them healed.

f.w: whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead

n: Jesus is the stone the builders rejected that has become the cornerstone. The “builders” — Israel’s leaders — are sitting right in front of Peter.

f.w: the stone which was set at nought of you builders
f.g: set at nought = treated as worthless.
The cornerstone that aligns and supports the whole building.

n: Salvation is found in no one else; there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved — a central declaration of Christian faith echoed in the Book of Mormon.
The leaders are amazed at the boldness of these untrained fishermen and realize they had been with Jesus. Time with the Lord had changed them.

f.g: Without formal rabbinic training; “ignorant” means ordinary, laymen — not stupid.

n: With the healed man standing right there, they have no rebuttal.

f.w: they could say nothing against it

n: They send the apostles out of the room and confer privately.

f.g: Luke may have learned of the private discussion from a sympathizer like Paul, once a Pharisee, or another council member.

n: They admit the obvious: a remarkable miracle has been done, all Jerusalem knows it, and they can’t deny it.
Rather than respond to the evidence, they decide to threaten the apostles severely so the movement spreads no further.

f.g: straitly = strictly, severely.

n: They call them back and order them not to speak or teach at all in Jesus’s name.

f.w: commanded them not to speak at all

n: Peter and John reply: you judge whether it is right before God to obey you rather than God.

f.w: hearken unto you more than unto God

n: They simply cannot stop speaking about what they have seen and heard. True witnesses can’t keep silent.

f.w: we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard

n: After more threats, the council releases them, unable to find a way to punish them without angering the people, who are praising God.
Luke notes the healed man was over forty — a lifelong condition, making the miracle all the more striking.

f.g: A detail that underlines the impossibility of a natural recovery.

n: Released, they return to their fellow believers and report everything the leaders said.

f.g: Their fellow disciples, the believing community.

n: Hearing it, the believers pray together with one voice to the sovereign Creator of heaven, earth, and sea.

f.w: thou art God, which hast made heaven, and earth, and the sea

n: They quote Psalm 2, spoken through David: why do the nations rage and peoples plot in vain?

f.g: heathen = nations, Gentiles; vain = empty, futile.

n: The kings and rulers of earth gathered against the Lord and his Anointed — his Messiah.

f.g: Christ = the Anointed One, Hebrew Messiah.

n: They see the psalm fulfilled: Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the people of Israel all united against God’s holy servant Jesus.

f.g: child = servant (Greek pais), as in Acts 3:13.

n: Yet they only accomplished what God had already determined would happen. God’s purposes prevail even through his enemies’ actions.

f.w: thy hand and thy counsel determined before

n: They don’t pray for safety or for the threats to stop — they ask for boldness to keep speaking God’s word.

f.w: with all boldness they may speak thy word

n: And they ask God to keep stretching out his hand to heal and perform signs through Jesus’s name.
When they finish praying, the building shakes, they are all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they speak God’s word boldly. Their prayer is answered immediately.

f.w: spake the word of God with boldness

n: The believers are united in heart and soul. No one claims private ownership of possessions; they share everything.

f.w: of one heart and of one soul

n: With great power the apostles testify of the Lord Jesus’s resurrection, and God’s abundant grace rests on them all.

f.w: gave the apostles witness of the resurrection

n: No one among them is in need, because those who own land or houses sell them and bring the money — fulfilling the ideal of Deuteronomy that there be no poor among them.

f.w: Neither was there any among them that lacked

n: They lay the money at the apostles’ feet, and it is distributed to each as they need. Laying something at someone’s feet signaled giving it into their authority.

f.w: laid them down at the apostles' feet

n: Luke introduces Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, whom the apostles nicknamed Barnabas, “son of encouragement.” He will become an important missionary companion of Paul.

f.g: consolation = comfort, encouragement, exhortation.
From the tribe of Levi, which traditionally served in temple duties.

n: Barnabas sells a field he owns and lays the money at the apostles’ feet — a model of generous consecration that sets up the contrasting story that follows.
